expanded_sentences: A 53-year-old female with confirmed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (T2 N2 M1) presenting with progressive respiratory symptoms including severe chronic dry cough and exertional dyspnea.
Patient has a documented history of tobacco use with 15 pack-years of exposure, having quit 7 years prior to diagnosis.
Elevated serum AST and ALT levels were observed during systemic therapy monitoring, with no prior history of hepatic disease.
Genomic testing confirmed the presence of an EGFR exon 19 deletion in tumor tissue, which is a known actionable biomarker.
CT-guided core biopsy of the right upper lobe lesion confirmed lung adenocarcinoma with no evidence of small cell features.
Baseline serum CEA level measured at 42.7 ng/mL prior to initiation of first-line systemic therapy.
The patient's mother has a history of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer diagnosed at age 61.
Current treatment regimen includes osimertinib 80 mg oral administration as targeted therapy for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
Imaging studies include recent computed tomography of the chest for disease assessment.
Liver metastases are documented as part of the M1 stage classification per TNM staging system.
